concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 5 – Uniformity Validation (Task 5.1); spec.md SC-005
concerns.text: Phase 5 runs scipy.stats.kstest on the raw p-values from the ACTUAL Möbius data, but SC-005 requires uniformity 'under the null hypothesis (simulated on random data)'. Testing the real data conflates null-validation with hypothesis-testing: if μ genuinely deviates from the random-sign model, KS will reject and the plan provides no way to distinguish 'test is broken' from 'null is false'. The validation must be run on synthetic random-sign windows (or on the permutation statistics themselves), not on the observed p-values.

KS test is invalid for discrete p-values. With exactly 1,000 permutations the two-sided p-value takes at most ~501 discrete values on a 1/1001 grid; a KS test against continuous Uniform[0,1] on such a lattice will spuriously reject at large n (≈5.56 M tests). Use a test appropriate to the discrete lattice (e.g. chi-square on binned counts, or KS against the empirical discrete null via simulation), or run the KS on a small subsample of independent lags/windows as the spec's 'approximate KS test' suggests.

Sensitivity uses raw p < 0.05 as the significance criterion while the main analysis reports BH-adjusted p-values as governing significance (research.md Limitations). FR-007 does say p < 0.05, but the plan should state explicitly that the sensitivity criterion is deliberately the raw threshold and why, otherwise 'significant_change' flags will fire on lags that were never significant after FDR — inflating apparent sensitivity.
